items.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018
items.q: it was Mrs. Marge and she pulled me aside... 'One day you are going to be a great singer.'... it was like that was the first person who told me, basically they hear something. To hear something in my voice. To hear something that has potential for something.

ctx.x: Well spell it and maybe it will help.

I don’t know how to spell it. I was five. I don’t know how to — but it was Mrs. Marge and she pulled me aside and she was like, “Alicia, I’m going to tell you something.” She was like, “You’re not going to know what this means right now, but one day you’re going to understand.” And I was like, “What’s that Miss Marge.” I thought I was in trouble. She said, “One day you are going to be a great singer. But remember, do not get the big head.” And I was like my head’s going to get — I mean I thought she meant like…

That’s terrific. Have you developed sort of an inner alarm when something comes, an opportunity in your career and you feel like tempted to do it and then say wait a minute, let me think about this. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
